subject: Product rights: evidence request to lock training restriction and usage boundaries
raw_thread:
From: Sofia Vega <sofia.vega@novatech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@novatech.com>, Procurement <procurement@novatech.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Product rights - evidence to support training restriction

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. Our legal team asked me to consolidate one list of what Redwood can provide as evidence that customer data will not be used to train generalized models and what operational controls would be contractually obligated. Specifically they want:

- Definitive language we can include in the Order Form and a short justification for each clause.
- An operations playbook snippet that describes how KV/prefix caching is isolated and when customer prompts are retained vs. dropped.
- A list of telemetry artifacts and logs you can provide for audits (timestamps, request ids, token hashes, redaction lineage).
- Clarification on feedback/license: whether feedback submitted in-product would be subject to any use outside the customer project.

I have attached a working redline of the Order Form (orderform_v2_redlines.pdf) and a template evidence manifest we use internally — see evidence_manifest.xlsx. Can you confirm whether the proposed Order Form wording below captures Redwood's guarantees, or propose alternative text?

--- proposed Order Form language (from NovaTech legal) ---
1) Service will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train or improve any model used by Redwood for generic or third-party services.
2) Customer shall retain exclusive rights to Customer Outputs; Redwood will not claim ownership.
3) Feedback submitted by Customer users via in-product channels may be used to improve the Service only with explicit opt-in.

We'd like to lock this in before we proceed to signature — procurement is holding budget pending legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Sofia Vega
Head of Platform Partnerships
NovaTech

>
> Hi Sofia — appreciated the call. High level answers and next steps below so we can give Legal what they need.
>
> 1) Order Form language: the three bullets look good as a customer-friendly starting point. We should refine the feedback line to make opt-in explicit and to define "use" to exclude internal feature experiments unless separately consented. I propose: "Feedback provided by Customer or Customer Users will not be used to improve or train Redwood's public or general-purpose models absent explicit, documented opt-in by Customer."
>
> 2) Evidence & ops artifacts: we can provide an evidence manifest that maps contractual guarantees to artifacts. Examples: caching isolation diagram (pdf), KV cache retention policy (markdown), redact/retention logs (CSV export), and a short runbook on model-variant routing and fallback. I'll attach the manifest from our Legal/Trust folder (see evidence_manifest.xlsx).
>
> 3) Audit artifacts: we can commit to providing a monthly extract of request metadata (redacted tokens, request ids, model variant used, timestamp) for the first 12 months post-deploy and on-demand exports for audits thereafter (subject to standard e-discovery process).
>
> 4) Operational guarantees: for customers who require hard guarantees, we offer Dedicated pools or Private deployments. Those can be scoped in the Order Form as an optional line item with stronger isolation and a separate SOW.
>
> Action items: Karthik, can you produce the KV isolation diagram and the retention policy by EOD tomorrow? Marissa, I'll need a short blurb from Legal / Trust to include in the Order Form justification section (2-3 sentences).
>
> Ben
>Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
>ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
>
>Attachments: orderform_v2_redlines.pdf

For customers requiring cryptographic proof of non-use, Redwood is willing to discuss scoped attestation processes under a separate SOW.
